summary_plain: Bull fixed his plan: he now waits for a dip to 158.76 and aims for one goal at 159.00 that pays 1.6 for each 1 risked, and he admitted the odds are thin. Bear attacked Bull's older plan (they wrote at the same time), so some of his points no longer apply, but his main message still holds. The desk replayed Bull's new plan 10,000 times: the goal came first only 36 times in 100 and the stop came first 62 times, while it needs about 38 to break even. In real history the goal came first 13 times and the stop 33 times, so it is still about a coin flip that loses a little on average.

best_point_plain.bull: He listened to the desk, dropped the goal that paid too little and rebuilt the plan so it pays 1.6 for each 1 risked, and he honestly said it is a thin trade.
best_point_plain.bear: Even with a better plan, no version the code tried has a real edge: the price is stretched, the short charts are fading and the odds sit just under break-even.
